slot.brief: Given initial amount and fraction remaining after a time, use number of half-lives to find the half-life or the time required.

stem: A first-order reaction starts with $80$ mg of reactant; $10$ mg remains after $6$ h. What is its half-life?

verdicts.working: The amount falls from 80 mg to 10 mg, or to 1/8 of its initial value. That is three half-lives in 6 h, so the half-life is 2 h.

working:
$\dfrac{10}{80}=\dfrac{1}{8}=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3$
$6$ h corresponds to $3$ half-lives
$t_{1/2}=\dfrac{6}{3}=2$ h

Independent check: The amount falls from 80 mg to 10 mg, or to 1/8 of its initial value. That is three half-lives in 6 h, so the half-life is 2 h.
solution:
For a first-order reaction, $N/N_0=(1/2)^n$. Here, $10/80=1/8=(1/2)^3$, so 6 h corresponds to 3 half-lives.
$$t_{1/2}=\frac{6}{3}=2\text{ h}$$
